book_understanding.teaching_order: A textbook usually opens with 'HDI is a composite index of health, education and income published by UNDP since 1990' and lists Haq's four pillars separately. Here the video starts from the open question left by the previous video (development has no measure yet), turns development into human development, lets economists face 'which parameters count?', brings Haq's four components as the answer, teaches each with one picture, then re-opens the problem (how to measure them together) so that HDI arrives as the next answer; it then checks HDI back against the four components to show what it misses, and only at the end gives the institution and the year.
book_understanding.breakdown_rule: Each part answers the question the previous part left open (what is development made of, how can it be measured, what does the measure miss), and a list is taught one item at a time with one picture per item.

opening.what: Recalls the last video (growth vs development), then says knowing the difference is not enough: we need to know how development can be measured; a question mark drops under development.

moves.concept: economic development as quality of life = human development

moves.concept: Haq's four components of human development
moves.what: Economists faced a big question: which parameters count as development and which do not.

moves.concept: Haq's four components of human development
moves.what: A Pakistani economist, Mahbub ul Haq, untangled the puzzle through his analysis and research.

moves.concept: Haq's four components of human development
moves.what: Human development has four essential components: equity, sustainability, productivity, empowerment.

moves.concept: Haq's four components of human development
moves.what: 'Chaliye' we cover the four in detail, starting with equity.

moves.concept: equity
moves.what: When a country grows, the benefit reaches only a small percentage of people, so equitable distribution is needed so that every citizen benefits.

moves.concept: equity
moves.what: 'To ye baat hui equity ki': closes the part.

moves.concept: sustainability
moves.what: 'Matlab sirf itna hai': the human development opportunities the present generation has (physical, financial, environmental).

moves.concept: sustainability
moves.what: If we pass those opportunities to the next generation as they are, that is sustainable human development.

moves.concept: productivity
moves.what: A country's output is generated by its people; raise their productivity and output rises ('obvious si baat').

moves.concept: productivity
moves.what: This can be done if the government provides health, skills, education and food security.

moves.concept: empowerment: political democracy and economic liberalism
moves.what: People who can take decisions by their own will are called empowered.

moves.concept: empowerment: political democracy and economic liberalism
moves.what: To empower people they must be given two things: political democracy and economic liberalism.

moves.concept: empowerment: political democracy and economic liberalism
moves.what: Political democracy means people can choose representatives who work for their welfare.

moves.concept: empowerment: political democracy and economic liberalism
moves.what: Economic liberalism means freedom from excessive economic controls and regulations.

moves.concept: Haq's four components of human development
moves.what: One line: these were the four components Haq called essential.

moves.concept: HDI as the answer to the measuring problem: three dimensions
moves.what: 'But' even with the components defined, economists and bodies such as the UN, IMF and World Bank faced the question of how to measure them.

moves.concept: HDI as the answer to the measuring problem: three dimensions
moves.what: Combining all these measures into one index is very difficult in itself.

moves.concept: HDI as the answer to the measuring problem: three dimensions
moves.what: After continued effort an index capturing many dimensions was formulated: the Human Development Index, HDI.

moves.concept: HDI as the answer to the measuring problem: three dimensions
moves.what: HDI works on three dimensions: standard of living, health, education.

moves.concept: what HDI captures and what it misses
moves.what: Standard of living corresponds to equity, 'jabki' health and education correspond to productivity (the narrator's own mapping; doubtful for equity).

moves.concept: what HDI captures and what it misses
moves.what: So HDI does not capture sustainability and empowerment.

moves.concept: UNDP's first Human Development Report, 1990
moves.what: UNDP first introduced HDI in its first Human Development Report (HDR), published in 1990 under Haq's leadership.

moves.concept: HDI as the answer to the measuring problem: three dimensions

closing.what: The opening growth-vs-development picture returns with HDI in place of the question mark (over about 13 s with no recognised speech), then a teaser for the next video on calculating HDI and the playlist plug; no recap of four components vs three dimensions, no exam link.

narration.density: About 22 terms (economic growth, economic development, quality of life, human development, parameters, equity, equitable distribution, sustainability, human development opportunities, present and next generation, productivity, economic output, food security, empowerment, political democracy, economic liberalism, representatives, index, dimensions, HDI, standard of living, HDR, UNDP) in about 263 s, about 5 per minute. Comfortable for a UPSC or class 11-12 learner because each component gets 20-40 s and one picture; empowerment is the most abstract stretch, and there is no number anywhere (no HDI value, no country example).

talmel_summary: Picture and voice land together on 15 of 24 tiles, and the best ones act out the meaning rather than write it: the gold highlight spreads over the whole crowd on 'har ek naagrik', the opportunity box is handed down on 'next generation ... pass', and the MEASURE lines step out on 'measure'. When the picture leads it is by 1.3-4.5 s, mostly for text (definition lines, the DIFFICULT stamp, the empowerment label) and once for the gold circle before 'small percentage'. Weak: productivity and empowerment are carried by labels and callouts, the claim that HDI misses two components is shown only by missing lines, and the closing return picture falls in a 13 s transcript gap.

voice.notes: About 161 words per minute; calm storytelling tone ('is gutthi ko suljha diya') with a steady signpost rhythm ('ab baat karte hain ...', 'to ye baat hui ...') that matches the sidebar checklist. Each component opens with 'Mahbub ul Haq ka kehna hai', which gives authority but repeats. The economist's name is pronounced in several ways. The only number read is 'Year 1990'; 'three dimensions' is said in English. A long pause or lost stretch of about 13 s at 248-261 s.

game_ideas.player_does: Runs a small country for five years with a growth budget: each year drags coins to tax-free gains for a few, schools and clinics, skill centres, food rations, forest protection, voting booths and fewer licences.
game_ideas.process_happens: The crowd picture responds: the gold highlight grows from a few heads to everyone (equity), the output arrow thickens as health and education rise (productivity), the next-generation crowd's opportunity box fills or empties (sustainability), and choice bubbles appear over people (empowerment); four pillar meters move.
game_ideas.win: All four pillars above the line at the end, with output still rising.
game_ideas.lose: Pouring everything into gains for a few keeps most of the crowd dark and the equity pillar falls; cutting forests for quick output empties the next generation's box and sustainability collapses even though output looks high.
game_ideas.concept: Haq's four components of human development

game_ideas.player_does: Sorts policy cards (free midday meals, right to vote, solar instead of coal, skill training, removing excess permits, minimum wage, clean water for villages) onto the four pillars.
game_ideas.process_happens: A correct card lights its pillar's picture (gold spreads, box passes down, output arrow grows, ballot bubble appears).
game_ideas.win: Every card on a pillar whose picture it really moves.
game_ideas.lose: A wrong pillar stays dark and the card flips to show what it actually changes (e.g. 'right to vote' does not raise output directly; it empowers).
game_ideas.concept: Haq's four components of human development

game_ideas.player_does: Stretches HDI's measuring tape from each of its three dimensions (standard of living, health, education) to the pillar it measures, then marks the pillars the tape cannot reach.
game_ideas.process_happens: The tape snaps to a pillar it can reach and falls short of the others, which grey out with 'not in HDI'.
game_ideas.win: Health and education linked to productivity; sustainability and empowerment marked as not captured (keep the standard-of-living link open until the mapping is checked).
game_ideas.lose: Linking HDI to empowerment or sustainability shows the tape falling short and the index ignoring a forest cut or a missing vote.
game_ideas.concept: what HDI captures and what it misses

notes_questions.q: Economic growth aur economic development ko measure karne mein kya fark hai?
Mahbub ul Haq ke anusaar human development ke chaar components kaun se hain?
Equity ka matlab kya hai, aur growth ka fayda sab tak kyon pahunchna chahiye?
Sustainable human development mein present generation next generation ko kya pass karti hai?
Logon ki productivity badhane se economic output kaise badhta hai, aur sarkar isme kya kar sakti hai?
Empowerment ke liye kaun si do cheezein zaroori hain, aur unka matlab kya hai?
HDI ke teen dimensions kaun se hain, aur yeh kaunse do components capture nahi karta?
HDI pehli baar kisne, kab aur kis report mein introduce kiya?

checks_learned: For a list of parts taught one by one, keep a side checklist that brackets the current part and ticks finished parts (worked well here); a code check can require it when a list has 3 or more items taught in sequence.
A claim that something is missing ('HDI does not capture X') must be drawn: grey out or cross the uncovered items, not just leave them unlinked.
A mapping the narrator draws between two lists (HDI dimension to component) is a claim and must be checked against a source before it is drawn.
Real photos of real people, national flags and real emblems on screen must be replaced by generic drawings; flag any photo held on screen for a long time.
A highlight that picks a subset ('only a few benefit') must land on those words, not 4.5 s before.
Do not draw an equals sign between two concepts unless the source states they are the same.
A transcript gap of more than 5 s (248-261 s) over a closing picture flags lost narration.

teaching_best.why: The big question ('which parameters count?') is posed before the four components arrive, so the list is heard as an answer.
Each component gets one meaning line and one crowd picture; equity's cause chain (benefit to a few, so distribute to all) is acted out by the spreading gold.
HDI is introduced as the answer to a felt difficulty (how to fold four things into one number), not as a bare definition.
The new index is checked back against the earlier four components and what it misses is stated, linking new to old.
The opening question picture returns with HDI in place of the question mark, closing the loop.

teaching_weak.why: No number anywhere: no HDI value, no country, no India rank; even 'three dimensions' are names only, and the calculation is pushed to the next video.
Empowerment is about 45 s of definitions (own will, democracy, liberalism) with text labels; no situation or example of a person choosing.
The mapping 'standard of living = equity' is doubtful (income per head is an average, not a measure of how it is shared).
'Economic development can be called human development' is a simplification stated as fact and drawn as an equals sign.
No recap linking four components to three dimensions, and no exam link although both lists are common exam questions.
